title: Policy sim params and actionables
content:
Purpose:
This is a working companion doc for the policy-sim spreadsheet (policy-sim-2025-v2). The goal is to capture the assumptions, experiment design, quick heuristics and an incremental rollout plan for smart routing policies that mix spot, reserved/dedicated capacity and cross-region fallbacks. Keep lean — this is for product + infra to iterate on the model and ship a safe default policy.

High-level objective:
- Reduce per-token infrastructure cost by 15–30% for mid-tail traffic while maintaining 99.9% P99 latency SLO for premium customers.
- Provide safe automatic fallbacks so high-importance requests don’t hit preempted spot machines without a short, guaranteed path.

Key spreadsheet tabs (policy-sim-2025-v2):
- assumptions: price curves, preemption probability by region/hours, cold-start latency penalties, KV cache hit assumptions
- scenarios: traffic mixes (PLG, enterprise batch, enterprise interactive), token distributions, seq length pmfs
- run-matrix: simulated routing decisions, retry/backoff, failover times, observed latency/cost per scenario
- sensitivity: per-parameter sensitivity runs (spot preempt rate, cross-region RTT multiplier, burst multiplier)
- rollout-plan: staged traffic percentages and guardrail metrics

Core assumptions (start here when editing model):
1) Spot vs on-demand price: baseline ratio 0.35 (spot = 35% of on-demand) for DGX-like GPU families.
2) Spot preemption distribution: global average 7%/hour for long-running slices; asymmetric by region (us-west 9%, eu-west 4%). Use conservative +50% scenario for stress tests.
3) Cross-region egress & added latency: 20–40ms median RTT add for cross-region fallback, cost add = egress price (~$0.01 per GB) ignored for small token sizes but accounted in enterprise pro-forma.
4) Cold-start penalty: 150–500ms added P95 for model variant cold starts when scaled from zero; autoscaling buffer reduces this to ~50–200ms.
5) Cache effectiveness: prefix cache hit = 18% for chat-style workloads; include a param to sweep 10%–40%.

Routing policy knobs captured in the sheet:
- priority tiers: {dedicated-reserved, on-demand, spot-hedged, spot-deep} mapped to cost + reliability score
- region preference: same-region preferred, then regional pool, then cross-region soft-fallback (policy window)
- spot bidding groups: bid-high (short runs), bid-low (cheap long tail) 
- safety buffer: keep N slots warm per-customer-tier (N small for PLG, larger for Enterprise)
- retry/backoff: exponential backoff with a max of 2 retries before routing to on-demand fallback

Experiment design notes (what to run and why):
- Single-variable sweeps: vary spot preempt probability from 2%–20% and observe cost vs SLA hit.
- Mixed traffic runs: 60/30/10 PLG/enterprise-interactive/enterprise-batch to see cross-subsidy effects.
- Time-of-day sensitivity: run diurnal pattern where US peaks 18:00–02:00 UTC and spot volatility increases by +30% on peaks.
- Cross-region failover test: force us-west scarcity and allow cross-region to eu-west vs on-demand local; measure added latency and cost delta.

Representative simulation outputs (notes, not final numbers):
- Cheap aggressive policy (spot-first, 2 retries): lowers cost by ~28% in median but increases P99 latency violation events by 0.02% (from 0.05% -> 0.07%).
- Conservative hybrid (reserve critical + on-demand fallback, limited spot for low-priority): cost down ~12%, P99 steady at 0.045%.
- Region-arbitrage (route low-priority to cheaper region when price gap >20%): cost down additional 3–5% but increases median latency for those requests ~25ms.

Heuristic recommendations (initial defaults for shipping):
1) Customer-tier aware priority: premium customers -> reserved -> on-demand fallback; non-premium PLG -> spot-hedged with max 1 retry then on-demand.
2) Soft cross-region fallback only for non-latency-sensitive traffic. Tag routes with latency budget and only allow cross-region if budget >40ms.
3) Spot bidding strategy: use bid-high for short-latency jobs (<200 tokens), bid-low for long batch jobs.
4) Keep a small warm buffer per model-team (e.g., 2–10 warm slots) adjustable by SLA and observed QPS variance.
5) Enable automatic cache-first routing: check KV/prefix cache before any new allocation to reduce cost and cold-starts.

Guardrails and visibility to ship with policy:
- Hard SLA fallback: if P99 latency for a route moves above 1.5x target for 5 mins, suspend spot usage for that route.
- Cost anomaly detection: alert if per-request cost deviates >35% from rolling baseline for 30m.
- Observability: dashboard per-route with: per-token cost, P50/P95/P99 latencies, retry rate, spot-preempt count, cross-region rate.

Metrics to track during rollout:
- API-level: P99 latency, tail latency spikes frequency, error rate, retry-induced errors
- Cost-level: per-request compute cost, blended cost, spot-utilization % by pool
- User impact: rate of user-visible delay > Xms, support tickets related to slow responses

Rollout plan (phased):
- Canary (1% traffic, non-critical routes): 2 weeks monitoring window, guardrails active.
- Gradual ramp (10%, 25%, 50% over 6 weeks) with weekly review and sensitivity runs post-change.
- Enterprise opt-in: allow enterprise tenants to opt into conservative policy via console toggle (default: conservative).
- Emergency rollback: immediate global switch to on-demand-only routing for a model if guardrails trip.

Open questions / action items:
- Q: How do we price cross-region egress for embedding-heavy workloads? Who owns legal/contract implications for inter-region data transfer? (Action: @Ethan follow up with infra-billing + legal)
- Q: Should we add a route-level SLA budget field in the console to express latency tolerance? (Action: @Sofia prototype UI field)
- Action: Add intraday spot volatility signal to the sim (Connor) and re-run sensitivity matrix for 2024–2025 business months.
- Action: Product to draft default policy text for docs and SDK behavior (Maya).

Notes to reviewers:
- This doc intentionally keeps high-level heuristics; the spreadsheet contains detailed formulas and run outputs. Update the assumptions tab first when changing any price or preempt-rate baseline.
- Keep experimental results reproducible: commit random seed to the run-matrix tab and snapshot simulation inputs in linked_artifacts.

Quick links (to paste into meeting notes):
- Spreadsheet: gsheet:policy-sim-2025-v2
- Confluence primer: confluence:opt-routing-playbook
- Jira epic: OPT-412

End of doc — comments and quick edits welcome.
